eliminations: re-running the same trajectory disagreed with itself at rate 0.1667, above the 0.02 reproducibility margin
assessment.reason: The outcome is not a function of the trajectory: re-running the same trajectory returned a different result 16.67% of the time. Collisions here say nothing about the representation, because NO representation of the trajectory could predict this outcome. Extending the grammar would fit sampling variation.

environment.description: The adequate rule, but a base-satisfying trajectory goes wrong only 55% of the time, drawn fresh on every run. The representation is sufficient; the world is not deterministic.
environment.name: stochastic

grammar_immutability.note: LB-1 may propose a representation extension; it may not adopt one. The feature grammar is a source constant.

question: can the discovery layer detect when its OWN representation is inadequate, rather than merely when Morrison's ontology is?

criteria.detail: 6 of 6 environments received the verdict their construction warrants: adequate→ADEQUATE; inadequate_delegation→INADEQUATE; inadequate_timing→INADEQUATE; inadequate_unlocalised→INADEQUATE; noise_limited→NOISE_LIMITED; stochastic→STOCHASTIC
inadequate_delegation: nominated 'actor_id' (withheld: 'actor_id'), resolution 1.0; inadequate_timing: nominated 'timestamp' (withheld: 'timestamp'), resolution 1.0
inadequate_unlocalised: localised=False, best family 'elapsed' resolved only 0.5, proposal emitted=False
inadequate_delegation: held-out F1 +0.3641; inadequate_timing: held-out F1 +0.2897 (minimum +0.10)
the current grammar reaches held-out F1 1.0 on the adequate environment (minimum 0.95); a low score would mean the negative control was not testing adequacy
a representation-extension proposal was emitted only for environments that are genuinely beyond the grammar
